problemSignature.symptom: targeted local DRC-repair route candidates can hang before final report emission
problemSignature.observedHelperProcesses: orphaned KiCad Python helpers after shell timeout

rootCause: The exact finisher executes multiple physical KiCad candidate mutations inside one KiCad Python helper. Some local bridge/via candidate geometries can wedge during board mutation, KiCad DRC, or related KiCad internals before the normal report writer runs. A subprocess timeout around kicad-cli DRC is not sufficient if the hang happens elsewhere in the helper.
fixSummary: Added target-net filtering, local DRC-repair bridge candidates for short leftovers, optional candidate zone-fill skip, and DRC timeout reporting. The next required hardening is to execute each physical candidate in an isolated child process with a hard timeout and parent-owned rollback/report aggregation.

testsAdded: exact finisher generates local DRC-repair bridge candidates for short leftovers

conditions: direct route reduces unconnected but creates local DRC
candidate geometry can hang before report emission
remaining board is DRC-clean but exact routing is exhausted

recipe: Filter exact finishing to one target net when debugging a known local blocker.
Prioritize local repair bridge candidates for short pad-to-pad leftovers.
Treat DRC timeout as a rollback reason, not as a final state.
If helper hangs before report emission, terminate orphaned helper processes and do not promote the candidate board.
Implement next generation as parent-supervised per-candidate subprocess execution with hard timeout and durable progress files.
safetyRules: Do not promote candidate boards without a current DRC report proving zero violations and reduced unconnected count.
Do not export manufacturing while unconnected items remain.
Do not touch protected ESC/FC projects.
Do not globally suppress DRC or hide timed-out candidates.
